content.text: The bug was introduced in commit `fee02a3d16aa835c2f1e606897e4bd08e51ba7d5`, which first added the `listMembers()`/`getMembers()` method with an empty `wrapUp(GHUser[] page)` body — never calling `GHUser.wrap(page, root)`.

This confirms it: prior to this commit, `getMembers()` called `root.getUser(login)` per item, which internally fully populates the user (that's why the old code had a comment about it being "shallow" but then fetched the full user via `getUser`). The refactor to `PagedIterable`/`PagedIterator` in this commit dropped that full-population step and left `wrapUp` empty, so returned users were never populated with full field values — exactly the bug later fixed in 6e9ec7a.

The subsequent commits (628034a, 9930e7b) only modified the URL/filter parameters and preserved the same empty `wrapUp` body, so they carried the bug forward but didn't introduce it.

## Reasoning
**(1) Investigation:** I ran `git log -p --follow` on `GHOrganization.java` to trace the history of the `getMembers()` method and the `wrapUp` override that the fix commit touches. I looked for when the empty `wrapUp(GHUser[] page) { }` body (with no call to `GHUser.wrap`) was first introduced.

**(2) Specific change:** Commit `fee02a3d` ("Support paging when fetching organization members") rewrote `getMembers()` from a `List<GHUser>` implementation — which called `root.getUser(shallow[index].getLogin())` per element, fetching a fully-populated user object — into a `PagedIterable<GHUser>`/`PagedIterator<GHUser>` implementation. In doing so, it introduced an empty `wrapUp(GHUser[] page)` method that does nothing, discarding the previous per-item full-population behavior. This means the `GHUser` objects returned from the paged API response are left "shallow" (partially populated from the list endpoint) with no lazy-loading root reference wired in, causing NPEs when calling methods like `getCreatedAt()`.

**(3) Evidence:** The fix commit `6e9ec7a` diff shows the exact same `wrapUp` method body being changed from empty to `GHUser.wrap(users, root)`. Looking at the diff of `fee02a3d`, that's precisely where this empty `wrapUp` body was created — and it remained unchanged (only cosmetic URL/param changes) through `628034a` and `9930e7b` until the actual fix. There's no intermediate commit that alters the `wrapUp` body's content, confirming `fee02a3d` as the sole point where the population logic was dropped.

I'm confident in this conclusion — the code evolution is linear and well-documented via commit messages, and the empty `wrapUp` body traces directly and unambiguously back to `fee02a3d`.
